title: Resume a halted mission from Needs you: the halt names the scenarios that are gone, and the page records the human's resume of exactly that halt, once
prompt:
Read web/src/home.ts (`needsYou`: the halted mission's item, today a command to copy) and web/src/missions.ts (`normalizeMissions`); crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs: the module comment (the two writes a person makes from the page, their guards and the `spawn_human` login), `input` and `write_body`; crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs (`halt_reason`, the scenario floor, the `task.gated` record); crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql (`spawn_mission_resume`, `spawn_human_input` and its grants, the fold of `mission.resumed` and of `task.gated`'s `scenarios`); crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs (`MISSION_BOARD`).

The problem. A halted mission is the one item in Needs you that the owner can only act on from a shell: the page shows the reason and a command to copy (`spawn mission resume --id N`). On 2026-11-10 mission #6 halted with "the scenarios fell from 111 to 32" and stayed halted about 7 h. The drop was intended (the journeys had replaced 001-090), but the halt did not say which 79 scenarios were gone, so telling an intended replacement from a candidate deleting the scenarios that judge it took a look at the tree.

Required behaviour.
(a) /api/missions: every mission carries `halt`. It is null when the mission is not halted. Otherwise it is {`event`: the id of the mission's latest mission.halted record (the halt it is in), `reason`, `at_ms`, `gone`}. `gone` is set for a halt on the scenario floor: the scenario file names (the gate directory's *.sh) that the directory held at the gating that set the floor and does not hold at the halt, sorted. It is null for any other halt. The integrator records what this needs: the names on the gating's record and `gone` on the halt's record. A resume starts a new floor, as today.
(b) Needs you: a halted mission's item (web/src/home.ts `needsYou`) carries `resume` {mission, halt: the halt's event}, and the Home page offers a Resume button on it that posts (c). The command to copy stays. The item's detail is the reason, followed, when scenarios are gone, by at most five of their names and "and N more" for the rest. Its `full` names them all. The page reads `halt` through `normalizeMissions`.
(c) `POST /api/mission/<id>/resume` with {"halt": <event>, "key": <idempotency key>} (the key may come in an `Idempotency-Key` header, as for an input).
- It has the guards of a person's input, in the same order: the read guard, POST only, the page's own Origin (or the token), the owner's own client when no token is set, JSON, a bounded body.
- `{"probe": true}` passes them and writes nothing (200).
- It runs as the `spawn_human` login through one new right, which may do nothing but this.
- For the mission's current halt it answers 202 {"event": <the record>} and records {"type": "mission.resumed", "id", "by": "human", "halt"}. That record folds exactly as the owner's resume does.
- The same key again is the same resume: 202, the same event, nothing new.
- It answers 409 with the reason in "error", recording nothing, when the mission is not halted ("not halted"), or is halted on another halt than the one named (a page not refreshed since).
- It answers 404 for no such mission, and 400 without a key or without a halt.
(d) Nothing else changes: `spawn mission resume` (the owner's) still works as today, and so do the halt rules and the alert of a halt, which clears on the human's resume as on the owner's.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/051.sh. A real loop runs one resident of one gated mission on a fake engine. `spawn serve` serves the API. One `spawn integrate` judges through a gate that accepts. The gate directory holds a.sh to e.sh. Task A lands with the floor at 5. Then c.sh, d.sh and e.sh are removed, and the mission halts ("the scenarios fell from 5 to 2").
- (1) /api/missions: the halt's event, its reason, and gone ["c.sh", "d.sh", "e.sh"].
- (2) `needsYou` under node alone, over that answer and over fixed cases (twelve gone; another reason; a mission not halted): the item's resume, detail and full.
- (3) Refusals record nothing: text/plain 415, another site 403, a probe 200, no key 400, no halt 400, no mission 404, another halt 409.
- (4) The resume: 202, the record by human for that halt, the mission no longer halted (also in /api/missions), the halt's alert cleared on that record.
- (5) The same POST again is the same event. A new key is 409 "not halted".
- (6) Task B lands (floor 2), b.sh is removed, and the mission halts again with gone ["b.sh"]. A resume naming the first halt is 409; one naming the second resumes it.
It fails with 1 at (1) on ea3a2e9f: /api/missions has no `halt`.

The product reason. The owner sees why a mission stopped and what went missing, and resumes it from the item that says so, on the halt they were shown, without a shell. A retried click resumes once. A stale page cannot resume a halt the owner has not seen.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base, any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host. Keep every existing check green and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
